openings:
The strongest opening is local. Its clients are dental practices, yet Local scores 0, the Horus read treats it as not a local market agency, and nothing in the record covers LSAs, Sponsored Places or map listings. A rival that sells implant practices local ads and map demand, priced per booked consult, is likely, moderate confidence, to win practices that bought its websites and search. Falsifier: a local ads or listings service page, or a case study with local results, at the next compile.

Price is the second lever: Monsoon puts displacement at 68.9 on an SMB book whose most movable hours are web builds and SEO, so an offshore delivered website and SEO package is likely to undercut it line by line. With no public pricing, an outcome priced offer goes uncontested in public, and the machine readable layer of schema and entity work for implant practices is unclaimed. Its proof is thin, case study pages repeating a name over boilerplate: prospects should be asked which results they have seen. The Closing Institute is the hardest part to copy: a rival is more likely to win by competing on the marketing half than by fighting its sales training.
